items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889; Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911; main creamery 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: paid by butterfat found by test, not weight; own station's test governs (story 1).
'under payment by weight, a faulty test would have cost nobody anything' (story 1).
Loomis secretary from 1901 (story 1), Teague bookkeeper (story 6), Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green (story 1).
'His son Selby managed the Association from 1913 to 1938.'
Station-gain line, 5 1/4% as usual, carried to the general account; 1898 entry quoted (story 6). Run dates the column from 1897, which is consistent with the key's ledger column.
Seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, fixed 17.6 c.c. charge into a bottle ruled for it, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. Core fact present.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice table, 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6, total $77.93.
'The real deficiency was 0.19 in every month, summer and winter alike' (story 4).

Section A says the pipette is 'the plant's own standard' and the error was invisible from inside, but never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and there was none in the county. The burette point appears only in Section F.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Bench routine and the test book (begun 4 May 1896, exhibit 1) described. Thin but the gated element is there.
1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass and recorded 3.61 thereafter are both given in Section A.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then 3.61, '?' entry (story 5).
Orra Brant, Emmet's sister, married Keddie; Emmet the largest patron (story 3).

1919 circular present, but the 17 March 1925 statement is given only as 'never taken cream'. Missing that he tested as taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are. Both bolded parts are required.
Died February 1934 uncleared; test book to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Six farms; Emmet's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 Jan 1897; the two scales always agreed.
Complaints from 1902. The two gaps are kept apart: 0.17 against Larrow Green's 3.78, 0.19 the true shortfall.
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908; the hay explanation is reported as its finding and then refuted.
200,000 lb at 3.42 (story 3); proportional loss, 4.56 short 0.24 against 3.42 short 0.18 (story 8).
Roy after 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel from 1962.
The key says the ridge gates the point. The run says only 'over the ridge' and never names Redlow Ridge anywhere. Cudd and Vessey County are present.
From 1915, four Hessel Bottom men hauled there each summer.
Cudd's own new glassware plus the Alder Corners figures/table (artifact) and Vessey County: at least two elements.
16 seasons 1915-1930, same herds about 3.80 against the station's 3.61.
Same herds' summer milk tested 3.80 at Alder Corners, used against the hay theory (story 4, story 8).
Figures obtained from Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, 1958.
Gives 'since 1907' in story 2 but never the 1936 end of the circuit in Section A, and story 7 contradicts the start with 'every visit from 1908'. The bolded span 1907-1936 is not stated.
Lactometer on every visit, never found added water (story 7).
12 June 1923, burette, whole lot condemned.
'Strawn wrote down the condemnation and nothing more.'
Ordered 28 June, reply 2 July, in use July; 1924 average 3.80; nobody connected it.
Crate to the loft; notebooks in the Farland library since 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, second and third sittings in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); 'found no cause established'.
Four books listed, including Strawn's 1923 notebook holding the condemnation, which nobody laid beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April; 4 May award of $3,800 'without admission', no cause established; charged to the station account (story 6).
One fifth of $19,000 (story 8); charged to the same station account as the gain (story 6).
Ivy b.1931, Ansel's granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Vaught.
Story 8 lists the records she gathered but never says they had never been brought together. That idea appears only in Section G, and credit does not travel into A.
February 1958, loft, nine survivors.
9 March, burette, 16.72 against 17.6, ratio 0.95; 0.88 c.c. short given in story 2.
One part in twenty from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.80 against 3.61; 0.19; proportional.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c; the ledger table shows the gain equals the 76,000 (story 6).
Bulletin 471, October 1958, clears him; '24 years' after his death. List item, so the core fact is enough.
Granddaughter.
Derived via Duncan, son of Ansel; great-niece rejected.
Second cousins with the full derivation.
A08: 'cannot be finally settled' (leans full), and second cousins either way. A correct abstention.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rejected.
Gideon wrote Article VII making the station test govern pay; Selby blamed patrons for his father's system. Also the Jerseys at 4.56.
A01: the headline verdict is 'The Vose and Keddie families: no relationship', resolved on Duncan's denial. That is an assertion, not an abstention.
Asserting either way scores 0. The run also treats a family member's denial as settling the matter, contrary to the key.
76,000; 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of delivered, each denominator named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
A02: cannot be determined; the recollections conflict.
Variable: the station's measuring glass, borrowed in place of its own; the only thing changed.
Tester, herds, pasture, scales, acid, bottles and more held constant.
3.80 for nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July.
Cause in the apparatus, not milk or man; limits given (which piece, how short).
Ledger (Teague/Kyle/Sill), 1911 (Keddie's book), 1923 rise (Strawn), Alder Corners (Rosalie): three or more narrators.
Independence argued; the ledger and 1911 hold without 1958.
A09: headline verdict 'No, so far as the sources show', siding with Kyle and dismissing Teague's 1916 claim. An assertion.
Yes, he knew the Hollow tested low (1902 complaints, 1919 circular).
Manager from 1913, signed the gain sheets, 1919 circular, argued water in 1925: three or more.
A03: 'no evidence that he knew they were wrong ... His conduct is that of a man who ... misattributed it, not one who knew'. A verdict on the understatement question.

1908 sampling (row 36), 1924 average (row 11), weigh-book start (row 23), farms (row 24), Orra's birth (row 33) and others, each resolved with a method. Circular count (row 25) left unresolved, no credit.
Explicit two-carrier list with breakers: NT-1 16.27, NT-11 12 July, NT-14 $77.39, NT-2 3.16, and more.
A04 (row 7, works books burned 1931), A06 (row 20, cannot be settled; Roy's pole eliminated on dates), A10 (row 26).
Self-refutations identified: r07 swap, r05 1905/1898, r15, r18, r20, r03, r11.
16.72/17.6, 95%, proportional; onset 1897 against 1896 at 3.80; cessation June 1923 with 1924 at 3.80; nothing on the farms changed.
Water (Vose, Sill) defeated by Strawn's lactometer, Cudd, the ledger surplus.
Theft (Teague, Oram's father) defeated: the cream arrived heavier; 1911; 1923 rise under the same tester.
Hay defeated: Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter, nil in summer, against 0.19 in every month; Alder Corners; winter-only sampling.
A07: the headline verdict is 'No.' An assertion.
A05: headline verdict 'He suspected the glass but could not prove it'; later hedging does not undo it.
About 138 words.
By-laws, invoice, weigh book, ledger, Strawn's condemnation, Alder Corners tests, test book (1911 weeks): five or more.
Decoys reported only as what the valley blamed; no wrong headline figures.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts the Alder Corners cheese factory 'was built in 1913' as fact (story 8; E row 38 'Built 1913'). The key catalogues 1913 (r10) as a planted error.
Corruption: 'Keddie went up in 1895' stated unhedged (story 1). This is the planted 1895 start (r01, r17), and the 1895/1896 conflict is never flagged.
Corruption: Strawn's circuit dated from 1908: 'tested with the lactometer on every visit from 1908' (story 7) and 'at every visit from 1908' (F2), stated unhedged. This is the NT-23 planted value.
Gullibility A01 (B4): asserts no Vose-Keddie relationship.
Gullibility A09 (D2): asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries.
Gullibility A03 (D3): asserts the manager did not know the tests were understated.
Gullibility A07 (F): asserts the board did not examine the glassware.
Gullibility A05 (F): asserts the tester suspected the glass.
